description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the reading and writing of files in standard formats.  Includes:
- Comma Separated Value (CSV).  Supports reading and writing CSV files with customizable delimiters. Ideal for CSV data normalization and transformation workflows.
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.
- `ICsvFileLine` is no longer an `IOrderedDictionary`. Field names are `string`, enumerating a line gives `KeyValuePair<string, object?>` items, `Keys` and `Values` are `IReadOnlyList<string>` and `IReadOnlyList<object?>`, and the `IDictionary` and `ICollection` members such as `CopyTo` and `SyncRoot` are gone.
- `CsvFileLineBase.Add` takes a `string` field name instead of an `object` key.
- A mapper registered with `RegisterMapper` applies only to the reader or writer it is registered on, not to every reader and writer of the record type; register it on each one. `CsvFileReader.Context.Mappers` holds only that reader's mapper.
- `CsvFileCacheRepositoryBase` and the `protected` members of `CsvFileIoBase<TRecordLine>` (`BuildException`, `DeserializeCsvLineFieldValue`, `DoesFieldValueRequireQuoting`, `GetCsvLineMappedFieldValue`, `GetMapper`, `NormalizeFieldValueLineBreaks`, `SerializeCsvLineFieldValue`) are removed, and `CsvFileIoBase<TRecordLine>` can no longer be derived from outside the package.
- Registering a mapper of another type with `RegisterMapper` replaces the registered mapper, where version 1.x kept the first one, and `UnregisterMapper<TMapper>` removes the registered mapper only if it is a `TMapper`.
- A mapped property with no converter is now parsed from its field (numeric, date, time, `bool`, `char`, `Guid` and enum types, their nullable forms, `IParsable<T>` types on .NET 10, and types with a `TypeConverter`), instead of reading as its default value.
- A field that fails to convert to a mapped property, with or without a `TypeConverter`, now goes to `BadValueHandler` or raises `CsvFileException`, instead of reading as the default value or throwing the converter's own exception.
- The `FieldIndex` that a mapped field's validator and `BadValueHandler` get is now the field's position in the line, not its position in the mapper's field names followed by the line's other names.
- When `BadValueHandler` is set, `CsvFileReader<T>` now returns the last field of a record that breaks the RFC 4180 quoting rules as an empty value, as it already did for every other field, instead of keeping its raw text.
- `CsvFileWriter<TRecordLine>.WriteLine` throws `ArgumentException` for a line that is neither a `CsvFileHeaderLine` nor a `TRecordLine`, instead of writing an empty record.
- `CsvFileWriter<TRecordLine>.WriteLine` throws `ArgumentNullException` for a null line, instead of writing an empty record.

New:
- `ICsvFileLine.IndexOf`, `TryGetValue` and `GetAt` find a field's position, read a value without a second lookup, and read the name and value at a position.
- `CsvMapperCache.Clear()` clears the process-wide cache of mappers built from `[CsvFieldMapping]` attributes.

Fixed:
- `CsvFileWriter<T>` no longer applies the `[CsvFieldMapping]` attributes of a line type derived from `T` to other lines of `T`, in the same writer or in any other reader or writer.
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- `CsvFileHeaderLine.FieldNames` returns the current names after a header field's value is replaced.
- With `CsvFieldQuoteHandling.Auto`, `CsvFileWriter` quotes a value that contains a line break, double quote or field delimiter even when it reads as a number, such as `1,000`.
- With no `Culture` set, `CsvFileWriter` formats values that have no converter with the invariant culture instead of the current culture.
- `CsvFileReader.ReadLine` throws the duplicate field names error again on every later call, instead of reading records against an empty header line.
- `CsvFileReader.ReadLine` throws the same exception again on every later call when the header line can't be read or a `HeaderHandler` throws, instead of reading the next record as the header line or skipping records.
- `CsvFileReader.ReadLine` throws `InvalidOperationException` when a `HeaderHandler` returns `null`, instead of `ArgumentNullException`.
- `CsvFileReader` no longer allocates memory quadratic in the length of the field when a quoted value is followed by many invalid characters.
- `CsvFileWriter` quotes a header name that holds a line break when `EmbeddedLineBreak` is set, and a value that holds a custom `TerminatorLineBreak`.
- `CsvFileWriter` with `QuoteHandling.Auto` no longer depends on the machine's culture to decide which values are numbers.
- the `CsvFileReader` and `CsvFileWriter` constructors that take a `TextReader` or `TextWriter` throw `ArgumentNullException` for null options.

Changed:
- The `netstandard2.0` build of File.CSV depends on `System.Memory` 4.6.3.
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- On the .NET Standard builds, a line no longer allocates an entry object for each field, and replacing the value of a field no longer invalidates an enumerator of the line, as on `net10.0`.
- `DataStandardizer.File.CSV` targets `netstandard1.1` instead of `netstandard1.3`, which gives it the same platform reach as the other packages; consumers on .NET Standard 1.3 or later resolve the `netstandard1.1` build.
